the prevalence of HIV in South Africa has increased from 10% in 2002 to over 20% in 2005 and that the prevalence is higher in women than in men, with women aged 25–29 having the highest prevalence.
HIV and ART are associated with a decreased likelihood of pregnancy in South Africa.

how HIV/AIDS is affecting the health, education, and social welfare of children in South Africa.
the impact of HIV/AIDS on the lives of children, adolescents and their caregivers in the Western Cape.
the effects of HIV on pregnancy outcomes, and with the effect of antiretrovival therapy on the pregnancy outcomes of HIV-positive women.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HIV epidemic is not a static situation and that it is important to understand how the epidemic is evolving in different populations in order to be able to design appropriate and effective interventions.
the HIV pandemic is a major public health issue in South Africa and the rest of Africa and that it is a major contributor to the burden of disease in South Africa.

the HIV epidemic is not only a health issue but also has important implications for the economic and social well-being of women and families in sub-Saharan Africa.
